Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1234 PM CDT Tue Aug 11 2026

Valid 121200Z - 131200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS PORTIONS OF
CENTRAL ILLINOIS INTO LOWER OHIO VALLEY...AND PORTIONS OF THE
CENTRAL PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe gusts and hail will be possible Wednesday
afternoon and evening across parts of the central and northern High
Plains. Damaging gusts and isolated hail will also be possible
across parts of the Midwest and Ohio Valley.

...Illinois/Lower Ohio Valley...
Forecast uncertainty remains high for these regions. Morning
convection, or lack thereof, will influence the location/magnitude
of afternoon severe potential. At least modest southwesterly flow at
low levels is expected to continue into Wednesday morning. It is at
least plausible that the boundary within Iowa/Illinois remains
stationary or makes only modest southward progress. Weak warm
advection may promote elevated storms in northern Illinois by mid
morning. These storms could produce large hail and isolated wind
damage. Into the afternoon, this activity could have a tendency to
develop southward into a very moist, destabilizing airmass in the
Lower Ohio Valley. Another possibility is the development along the
surface boundary during the afternoon. The eastward progress of
storms will likely be limited as substantial impact from convection
is anticipated from Tuesday afternoon/evening. Steep mid-level lapse
rates and 40-45 kt of effective shear will allow for organized
storms capable of isolated large hail and damaging winds. Damaging
winds are expected to be the main threat as upscale growth is
expected to occur quickly. The 15% Wind/Slight Risk has been
adjusted northward and eastward to account for trends in guidance
and expected airmass destabilization.

...Central Plains...
Moist, easterly flow north of a developing surface low in eastern
Colorado/western Kansas will allow for moderate to strong
destabilization across parts of Nebraska/southern South Dakota.
Steep mid-level lapse rates and moderate to strong effective shear
will promote supercell development from near the Black Hills to
southwestern Nebraska. Large hail and isolated severe wind gusts
would be possible initially. Some intensification of the low-level
jet may lead to upscale growth into one or more linear segments
moving eastward. The potential for a more organized MCS is not clear
given the low-level jet will be focused farther east. Elevated
storms associated with the low-level jet core are possible in
eastern Nebraska/western Iowa where large hail and isolated wind
gusts may occur.

...North Dakota into Wisconsin Michigan...
Modest destabilization is expected farther north into the northern
Plains and Upper Midwest/Great Lakes. Sufficient mid-level flow will
be present for organized storms. The main questions will be storm
coverage and longevity. Isolated wind damage and large hail would
occur with the strongest, sustained storms.

...Carolinas/southern Appalachians...
Uncertainty in the evolution of early morning convection remains
relatively high. While an MCV from convection in the Ohio Valley may
impact parts of these regions, the timing of this feature may not
lend to an organized severe threat during the afternoon. The
Marginal risk will be maintained this outlook cycle for potential
isolated strong to severe storms. However, the potential for
sufficient airmaass destabilization continues to appear low.

..Wendt.. 08/11/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0232 PM CDT Tue Aug 11 2026

Valid 131200Z - 141200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE FRONT
RANGE INTO THE MIDDLE OHIO VALLEY...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms are possible on Thursday from the central
High Plains into the Ohio Valley.

...Central Plains into Middle Ohio Valley...
Moderate to strong destabilization near and south of the surface
boundary appears possible by the afternoon. Deep-layer shear will be
stronger with eastern extent, but still mostly along and to the
north of the boundary. Given this flow orientation, convection will
likely tend to train along the front. Isolated strong gusts and wind
damage are the main concern, particularly with any clusters that can
develop and move into more buoyant air south of the boundary.
Additional storm development is probable as the low-level jet
intensifies during the evening, though storms will be more elevated
by that point.

...Front Range...
Moist easterly flow into the higher terrain will promote scattered
storm development during the afternoon, perhaps aided by a subtle
shortwave perturbation. While cloud cover may temper surface
heating, steep mid-level lapse rates will allow for 1500-2000 J/kg
MLCAPE. Deep-layer shear will be marginal, but a few strong to
marginally severe storms may produce isolated severe winds and hail.

...Northeast...
Wind fields aloft will strengthen as a mid-level jet crosses over
the region on Thursday. Despite long hodographs, drier conditions
(50s F dewpoints with perhaps pockets of low 60s F) will limit
destabilization along with weak to modest mid-level lapse rates. A
few stronger gusts and small hail could occur with the stronger
activity, but severe-caliber potential still appears low.

..Wendt.. 08/11/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0313 AM CDT Tue Aug 11 2026

Valid 141200Z - 191200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...D4/Friday...
Moderate to strong destabilization will again be possible on Friday,
near and south of a front extending from the central Plains and
Midwest into parts of the southern Mid-Atlantic. Considerable
uncertainty remains regarding the exact frontal position, but strong
storms will be possible in its vicinity. Most guidance depicts
rising midlevel heights and modest deep-layer flow/shear in the
vicinity of the frontal zone, which may tend to keep the severe
threat isolated. One possible exception will be in the Carolinas and
southern VA, where the glancing influence of a seasonably deep upper
trough over the Northeast may result in a somewhat more organized
severe threat, if sufficient destabilization can occur.  

...D5/Saturday - D6/Sunday...
Some dampening of the upper ridge (potentially aided by one or more
MCVs emerging from the High Plains) may result in severe potential
emerging this weekend across parts of the Upper Midwest and Great
Lakes/Ohio Valley. However, details regarding timing of any
shortwave troughs and position of the primary frontal zone remain
quite uncertain. 

...D7/Monday - D8/Tuesday...
Extended-range guidance generally suggests potential for a
northwesterly flow regime to develop from the northern Plains into
parts of the East by early next week. Predictability remains quite
low regarding the extent to which stronger deep-layer flow impinges
upon favorable instability, but at least isolated severe potential
may eventually develop from parts of the north-central CONUS into
the Mid-Atlantic and Carolinas.

..Dean.. 08/11/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0748 PM CDT Tue Aug 11 2026

Valid 120100Z - 121200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS OF
THE DAKOTAS AND NORTHERN NEBRASKA...AND FROM NORTHERN ILLINOIS TO
WESTERN NORTH CAROLINA...

...SUMMARY...
Severe storms posing a risk for large hail and damaging winds are
possible into tonight from the Dakotas into the Midwest.

...IL to western NC...

A bowing line of storms from central KY into northeast TN/western VA
will continue to develop southeast the next few hours. A damaging
wind risk will continue with this activity in the short term.
However, convection should begin to wane with southeast extent into
the Appalachians as instability wanes and loss of daytime heating
results in a cooling boundary layer. Convection across KY and
perhaps portions of eastern TN may remain stronger into the evening
given the large reservoir of instability ahead of storms, but
overall expected is for a gradual weakening trend. Reference MCD
1939 for more short term details.

Overnight, most CAMs guidance suggests convection will redevelop
within a warm advection regime across parts of northern IL into IN
and the Ohio Valley. The 00z DVN and ILX RAOBs depict an impressive
thermodynamic and kinematic environment. Midlevel lapse rates near 8
C/km amid 40 kt effective shear and MUCAPE near 5000 J/kg with weak
inhibition suggests any storms developing within this environment
could be severe. Convection may develop along the instability
gradient and large hail is possible. If sufficient clustering
occurs, damaging wind also could be possible. As a result, the
Slight (level 2 of 5) risk as been expanded back to the northwest
across northern IL.

...Dakotas into IA...

Supercells across the western Dakotas and far northern NE will
continue to pose a risk for very large hail and damaging gusts the
next few hours. See MCD 1938 for short term information on severe
risk. 

It is uncertain how convection will evolve longer-term during the
overnight hours. Some guidance suggests clustering will occur and an
MCS could develop, moving east/southeast across SD/northern NE and
perhaps as far east as IA. Ample west/northwesterly flow aloft is in
place, along with a very moist airmass with strong to extreme
instability. If sufficient clustering can occur, MCS
development/maintenance seems plausible. have expanded the Slight
(level 2 of 5) risk eastward across SD/NE into western IA border
vicinity for this possibility.

..Leitman.. 08/12/2026
